posts.name: Kaivax
posts.cooked:
Yesterday, we updated dungeon play so that experience gains in instances are nullified if a high level player is in the group and enemies are trivial to that player. For some dungeons, the new restriction missed the mark because of the overall level range of the enemies in the dungeon.

With hotfixes that are now live, we’ve just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so that the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies.

Please note that this adjustment will not apply in instances that were already underway when it was deployed (a few minutes ago).

Thank you very much!

posts.name: nathaniel
posts.cooked:
Good evening!

I was hoping for some support.

I picked up a quest at level 35 which takes me to Maraudon. Previously this dungeon was available to enter from level 30. After attempting at level 37, I am getting the message, “You are not high enough level for this Dungeon”. I’ve tried to find a resource to show the minimum level to enter dungeons but I cannot so any help would be appreciate.

There are a few reasons I wanted to enter this dungeon with one of them being an incredibly great wrist upgrade for leather users, alongside a potential quest reward of 11,100 XP.

The LFG tool shows Maraudon being 46-55, at which case this quest shouldn’t be able to be picked up if you can’t complete it… (Rot and Regret - Shendralar/Desolace).

Wowhead lists the dungeon as 42-52 for comparison.

Any information would be greatly valued!

posts.name: Nantro
posts.cooked:
How about, instead, you actually adjust the level ranges of the dungeons? It makes no sense for enemies at the entrance to be up lower than the final boss.

Instead of fixing this core issue, you’ve chosen the simplest and worst possible workaround. A blanket 12-level XP cutoff is just a lazy band-aid fix that creates massive frustration for normal leveling groups, causes players to randomly lose XP mid-run without clear in-game feedback, and punishes friends who want to play together. Perhaps it’s time to rethink these outdated design habits you’re constantly treating the symptoms rather than the root cause.

What was the point of having a beta, anyway? You are repeating the exact same mistakes here that turned Retail into a complete patchwork mess over the last few years. Instead of building solid, well-thought-out systems from the ground up, everything is rushed out half-baked and patched reactively on live servers—leaving the players to deal with the fallout of broken mechanics and constant hotfixes.

Ultimately, it is damage control; it doesn’t actually solve the problem, but rather shifts it elsewhere.
